items.name: Anthropic AI Usage Index (AUI), Anthropic Economic Index
items.note: The AUI measures whether Claude.ai use is over- or under-represented in an economy relative to its working-age population, where 1.00 is the expected level. Privacy-preserving analysis of sampled conversations. Measures one provider only, so it is a proxy for frontier AI adoption and not a total measure.
items.verificationNote: The Anthropic Economic Index publishes country-level usage data. The Rwanda figures here are as reported in the 2026 landscape review, which cites the country view of 26 June 2026; the underlying index page was not re-parsed.

items.name: Africa AI Governance Index (AAIGI) 2026 — Inaugural Report
items.org: Africa AI Policy Lab and Lawyers Hub
items.note: Published July 2026. Scores all 54 African states across 80 indicators in 8 pillars on a 0–4 scale, grounded in the AU Continental AI Strategy and the Malabo Convention. Supported by the Patrick J. McGovern Foundation. Rwanda 3.25 is the highest composite on the continent.
items.verificationNote: Publisher, scale, methodology and Rwanda's score of 3.25 confirmed against the primary report PDF and four independent secondary reports (Ecofin Agency, Africa Business Communities, africaainews, Lawyers Hub).

items.name: Government AI Readiness Index 2025
items.note: Assesses 195 governments across 69 indicators, 14 dimensions and 6 pillars: Policy Capacity, Governance, AI Infrastructure, Public Sector Adoption, Development and Diffusion, Resilience. The 2025 edition uses a revised methodology and is NOT comparable with the 2021 edition.
items.verificationNote: Publisher and country count confirmed against the Oxford Insights site and the 2025 report PDF. Rwanda's rank of 75 — with Kenya 65, South Africa 67, Mauritius 71 — corroborated by two independent secondary summaries.
